title: Switch from guitar to banjo and banjo versus guitar
summary: Guitars were universal around 1910, banjo took over about 1915, and he prefers banjo for its drive; chords are more complex today.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: I wonder if you can tell us about you say you started on guitar and then later switched to banjo. When you were a kid say ten years old were most of the bands using guitars or banjos?
Most of them or all of them you think?
All of them I've seen they were using guitars that time. That would be 1910 about. That's around 1910 they were all using guitars.
You know before that if they'd ever used banjo did your father or Simon or John ever say?
No Bill. It was a long time, long time after that. It was around 1915. Tomorrow remember that banjo did get popular.
Tomorrow remember that banjo did get popular.
Do you think John switched over about that time too? Do you know when you might have done it?
Yes, John switched over about that time too. From guitar to banjo.
He'd been playing guitar before then? He did play guitar yeah. And you switched then by 1917 your first job there along in there was on banjo. On banjo yeah.
But that time were almost all the bands using banjo or something else?

Oh yeah they were popular. You know banjo was a big thing in this town one time. If you couldn't play banjo they wouldn't hire you. The guitar was gone all just like the bass violins. Everybody switched then? Everybody switched. They switched the bass violins then the sousaphone come in style. They switched the sousaphone. The bass violins couldn't play the sousaphone he couldn't have no job.

Your father though never played sousaphone. No he never did. He died 1917. Around that time yeah Bill. But that time tubas weren't popular. No no no no. Which do you like best really? Banjo or guitar?

Bill I like the banjo not because I'm not much of a guitar player but I like the banjo for one reason. I think the banjo has more support to my own kind of music, jazz. It's more support to the band. More swinging. Yeah it's got a good drive.

I mean good drive. If you play it right and don't try to do too much. I mean it sounds good. Play with the fellas and compliment, give them the right compliment and the right chords. It sounds better. What I want to say Bill, when I was playing guitar it was different than now. Because the guys playing guitar now I never make a guitar player. Because a guitar is too hard now. You see all sorts of things as 13 chords. Yeah all those. And 10 and 9. We didn't have all those things. We didn't have all those different kind of chords. That's just added on to my feelings.
